text:
This source gives a specific rule of thumb for commercial harvest timing: cut the bunch when the fruit has reached roughly 75% (three-quarters) of full maturity/roundness rather than waiting for complete fullness in the field. Harvesting slightly under full maturity leaves enough ripening still to happen during the days needed for transport and market handling, so the fruit arrives at the point of sale properly ripened rather than overripe or starting to spoil.

As a practical check, farmers are advised to judge maturity primarily from the plumpness/roundness of the fingers (as also described in the newer MAFF manual) rather than from skin color, since color change happens later in the ripening process, largely after harvest. Because a mixed planting will have bunches maturing at different times, staggering harvest across a plantation rather than cutting everything at once also helps match the volume of fruit moving to market with actual buyer demand and available post-harvest handling capacity.
